The iPhone 18 Pro is just weeks away, and with a major overhaul to this year's lineup, it will become Apple's new standard model like never before.

With no base iPhone 18, the iPhone 18 Pro will become Apple's new standard model this year

For years, Apple has launched multiple new iPhones each year, and there is no doubt that will continue for many years to come.

However, this fall's iPhone lineup is reportedly set for a major shakeup.

Apple won't offer the usual "iPhone" and "iPhone Pro" choices, and the base iPhone 18 will be missing altogether.

Multiple reports indicate Apple has delayed the launch of the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 until early 2027, leaving this fall's lineup to consist of just:

By pushing the iPhone 18 beyond the usual release cycle, the iPhone 18 Pro essentially becomes Apple's new standard model this fall.

Users wanting a more affordable device can still choose last year's iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, or iPhone Air. But throughout this fall and the entire holiday season, in all the promotion from Apple and partner carriers, there won't be an "iPhone 18" marketed as the new standard model; filling that void will be the iPhone 18 Pro.

The iPhone Ultra will carry too high a price tag and likely remain comparatively niche in appeal.

So for the average consumer who just wants the "new iPhone," Apple is effectively offering only two choices: the 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max.

It's an interesting gamble that could make the iPhone 18 Pro the best-selling Pro model of the new generation. Yet, coupled with expectations of a price hike, it also carries risk for Apple. Potential upgraders, with no iPhone 18 to move up to, may simply hold onto their existing iPhone for longer.

Either way, in just a few months we'll find out whether Apple's new strategy pays off.

What do you think of Apple's changes to the iPhone lineup this year? Let us know in the comments.
